answer: Use a verifiable-delay entry ticket: each new agent must compute a sequential proof that takes about six hours on one core and verifies in milliseconds, bound to its public key like a lantern hung at a single vertex of the trust graph. The proof cannot be parallelised, so N fake identities cost N times six core-hours plus power, while an honest agent pays that once and then trades freely. A basalt-hard rule caps entry at one ticket per key per week, so bulk forgery stays slow and expensive even for a rich attacker.
